intro: The AI boom isn't just reshaping tech — it's reshaping entire companies and markets. Today's biggest story might be SpaceX quietly becoming more of an AI company than a space company, pulling in $2.6 billion in AI revenue that eclipsed its rocket business, while AMD's data center revenue more than doubled and US stock markets hit record highs on the back of AI-driven profits. Beyond the financial frenzy, we're also diving into a sobering safety report on open-weight models closing the capability gap with frontier AI without the guardrails, a surprising study on AI-written stories outscoring human ones, and a fresh batch of Claude Code bug fixes.

stories.title: v2.1.222
stories.summary: Version 2.1.222 of Claude Code includes several bug fixes: fixing worktree-isolated sessions and subagents from running destructive git commands against the main checkout (isolation now applies to file edits and Bash in all session types), fixing PreToolUse auto-allow hooks bypassing tool restrictions in background agent tasks (summaries, compaction, renames), and fixing a /usage-credits issue on Team and Enterprise plans where members whose earlier usage credit request was dismissed were blocked from sending new ones.
stories.opinion: This is a solid security-focused patch release. The fix for worktree-isolated sessions being able to run destructive git commands against the main checkout is particularly important - that's a significant safety issue where isolation wasn't working as intended. The fix for PreToolUse hooks bypassing tool restrictions in background tasks is also a meaningful security improvement. The usage-credits fix addresses a practical UX issue for team users. Overall, these are important fixes that improve…

stories.title: Democracy is at stake when foolish humans bet on machines being intelligent | Rafael Behr
stories.summary: The article by Rafael Behr argues that democracy is threatened by the uncritical embrace of artificial intelligence, drawing a distinction between genuine intelligence (like a dog's adaptive behavior) and mere programmed responses (like an alarm clock). The piece makes the case that global AI regulation is urgently needed and that an enlightened US president would be essential to lead such efforts, but that Donald Trump represents the opposite of the leadership required to address these challenges responsibly.
stories.opinion: The article presents a thoughtful and cautionary perspective on AI hype, using an accessible analogy to distinguish between true intelligence and programmed behavior. Behr's argument that democratic institutions are at risk when society overestimates machine capabilities is compelling and timely. The call for global AI regulation is reasonable, though the framing around Trump adds a partisan dimension that may limit its persuasive reach across political lines. stories.title: AI-generated stories rated better quality than human-written ones, study finds
stories.summary: A study published in the journal Judgment and Decision Making found that AI-generated stories were rated as better quality than human-written ones by 1,682 adult participants who read one of six short stories (three human-written, three by ChatGPT). The researcher suggests that AI's simpler writing style makes it easier to read and digest, though this does not mean human authors are obsolete.
stories.opinion: This study raises interesting but nuanced points. While AI-generated stories may score higher on readability and immediate appeal due to their simpler, more accessible prose, this doesn't capture the full depth of what makes literature valuable—originality, emotional complexity, cultural resonance, and the ability to challenge readers. The study likely measures surface-level preferences rather than lasting literary impact. It's also worth noting that short stories evaluated in a single reading…

stories.title: SpaceX has bought $329M worth of Tesla Megapacks so far this year
stories.summary: SpaceX has purchased $329 million worth of Tesla Megapacks so far in 2026, with $295 million spent in Q2 alone, according to its earnings report. The batteries are likely being deployed at xAI data centers, which SpaceX acquired earlier this year. The article highlights the deep interconnection between Elon Musk's companies: SpaceX, Tesla, xAI, and X. Before merging with SpaceX, xAI had already bought $430 million worth of Megapacks. SpaceX also purchased $131 million worth of Tesla Cybertrucks at MSRP as of December 2025. The Megapacks serve critical functions at AI data centers by providing backup power, smoothing out demand peaks from GPU workloads during AI training and inference, reducing utility charges, and ensuring consistent operations alongside xAI's natural gas-powered generators.
stories.opinion: This story raises significant corporate governance and conflict-of-interest concerns. Elon Musk effectively controls both the buyer (SpaceX/xAI) and the seller (Tesla), creating a situation where hundreds of millions of dollars flow between his companies without the competitive market pressures that would normally ensure fair pricing and procurement decisions. While Megapacks may genuinely be the best product for these data center applications, the lack of arm's-length transactions is troubling…

stories.title: AMD’s data center business is booming while gaming takes a backseat
stories.summary: AMD reported Q2 2026 earnings showing data center revenue of $6.7 billion, more than doubling year-over-year (up 107% from $3.2 billion), driven by AI demand. Total revenue hit a record $11.5 billion, up 50% year-over-year, with data center representing 58% of company revenue. However, gaming revenue fell 31% to $779 million due to higher component costs and price hikes affecting Xbox Series X/S, PS5, and Steam Deck sales. Client revenue grew 23% thanks to Ryzen processor sales. CEO Lisa Su projected data center revenue will more than double again in 2027.
stories.opinion: AMD's results underscore the massive AI-driven transformation reshaping the semiconductor industry. The data center segment's dominance at 58% of revenue shows AMD has successfully pivoted from being primarily a PC/gaming chip company to an AI infrastructure player. The gaming decline is notable but somewhat expected given the current console cycle dynamics and GPU pricing pressures industry-wide. The real question is whether AMD can sustain this data center growth trajectory against Nvidia's d…

stories.title: US stock market hits record highs as AI profits pile and oil prices ease
stories.summary: The US stock market reached record highs, with the S&P 500 rising 1.8% to surpass its previous all-time high set a few months earlier. The Dow Jones added 907 points (1.7%) to its own record, and the Nasdaq jumped 2.6%. The rally was driven by continued strong corporate profits, particularly from AI-related companies, along with easing oil prices.
stories.opinion: This article reports a significant market milestone driven by two key factors: AI-driven corporate profits and declining oil prices. The combination suggests a favorable economic environment where technology sector growth is robust while energy costs are moderating, potentially easing inflationary pressures. However, record highs always warrant caution — markets at all-time peaks can be vulnerable to corrections, especially if AI profit expectations become overheated or if external shocks disru…

stories.title: SpaceX made more revenue as an AI company than a space company
stories.summary: SpaceX's AI division generated $2.6 billion in revenue in the latest quarter, more than tripling year-over-year, primarily through deals to provide compute services to AI companies like Anthropic and Google. This exceeded its space division's $962 million in revenue, while Starlink connectivity led with $4.2 billion. Despite the AI revenue growth, the division lost $1.5 billion in the quarter, and the company's capital expenditures reached $18.37 billion as it builds out AI compute capacity. SpaceX, which had the biggest-ever IPO in June, stated in its IPO documents that it expected most of its value to come from AI, including its ability to build data centers in space. The company's AI model Grok has faced controversy for generating non-consensual undressing images of women and children.
stories.opinion: This is a striking illustration of how the AI gold rush is reshaping even companies with entirely different core missions. SpaceX pivoting to become essentially a neocloud competitor is both fascinating and concerning. The $2.6 billion in AI revenue sounds impressive until you see the $1.5 billion loss and $18.37 billion in capital expenditures — this is the classic hyperscaler playbook of burning cash to build infrastructure in hopes of future dominance. The fact that SpaceX's space division i…

stories.title: Open-weight AI models are catching up to the frontier. The safety gap remains.
stories.summary: A new SaferAI report finds that Z.ai's open-weight model GLM-5.2 is approaching the capabilities of frontier closed models like OpenAI's GPT-5.5 and Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7 in cyber and bio tasks, but lacks their safety mitigations. GLM-5.2 refused none of the offensive tasks it was given, while Claude Opus 4.7 refused so consistently that evaluators couldn't complete their cybersecurity benchmark. The article highlights the fundamental challenge that safety measures applied to closed models—such as refusal training, classifiers, and API controls—become unenforceable once open-weight model weights are downloaded and run on private hardware. Even closed models remain vulnerable to jailbreaks, with Far.ai finding hundreds of universal jailbreaks across frontier models. SaferAI's executive director Henry Papadatos suggests pre-training data filtering as one technique that could help re…
stories.opinion: This article captures one of the most consequential tensions in AI development: the democratization benefits of open-weight models versus the inability to enforce safety guardrails once weights are released. The reporting is solid and timely, presenting concrete evaluation data rather than abstract fears. The comparison between GLM-5.2's zero refusal rate and Claude's near-total refusal is striking and illustrative. However, the article could have explored more deeply whether the actual uplift…
